newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Advanced Medical buying IVAC Medical.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Advanced Medical buying IVAC Medical.

text.p: Advanced Medical Inc. said Monday it will buy IVAC Medical Systems Inc. for about $400 million in cash, creating one of the world's largest makers of intravenous infusion therapy products.
IVAC, a former Eli Lilly & Co. unit, will merge with Advanced Medical's unit, IMED Corp., to form a new company. The merged company will have estimated revenues of $353 million.
Eli Lilly sold IVAC on Dec. 31, 1994 to DLJ Merchant Banking Partners LP, River Medical Inc. and other investors.

The merger with Advanced Medical came about when those investors in IVAC wanted to cash out, said William Mercer, president and chief executive officer of IVAC, who will head the newly merged company.

"We had one of those situations that was really fortuitous, our financial investors, led by DLJ, were ready to exit and we had one of our competitors in the marketplace ready to acquire," Mercer said in an interview.

Advanced Medical has about 1,000 employees while IVAC employs some 1,600 workers. Both firms have about 500 workers in Mexico. Mercer said an unspecified number of jobs in both the U.S. and Mexico will be cut because of the merger.
"There is some overlap between the two companies," Mercer said. "There will be some job reductions related to the merger. We have some duplication in staff functions, manufacturing in particular."

Joseph Kuhn, who was president of Advanced Medical and will now serve as chief financial officer of the new company, said the company will seek out a strategic partner in Japan and other acquisitions to grow the company.

"We expect to grow the business going forward so I think you'll see consistent earnings growth as well as sales growth from the combined organization," Kuhn told reporters on a conference call. "We will obviously be doing other types of acquisitions to add to the product line."
"We would like to get to the level of being a moderate growth company ... approaching 10 percent sales growth numbers. That's what we're going to strive for in the future," Kuhn added.

Kuhn said the acquisition will be financed through a $315 million bank loan facility, $120 million of subordinated notes and $40 million of equity from Chairman and principle shareholder Jeffry Picower.
Advanced Medical said it expects to take an unspecified one-time charge to pay for the merger. It did not say when the charge would be taken.
The company's stock was up 44 cents at $2.875 on the American Stock Exchange Monday.

Advanced Medical, through IMED, specialzes in intravenous infusion pumps that regulate the amount of medicine being given to a patient through an intraveinous drip. IMED introduced the world's first volumetric infusion pump in 1974 and has sales in 38 foreign countries.
San Diego-based IVAC also makes infusion systems but also makes pulse, blood pressure and temperature products.
IVAC is best known for inventing the first electronic thermometer in the 1970's and the infra-red thermometer that takes temperatures from the ear.
IMED had profits of $1.7 million, or 6 cents per fully diluted common share, on $53.9 million in revenues in the first half of 1996.
Excluding the effect of a one-time restructuring charge of $17.4 million, IVAC had net income of $4.2 million on net sales of $112.8 million for the 1996 first half.
Advanced Medical reported profits of $8.4 million on sales of $29.2 million in the quarter ended June 30.
The deal is expected to close by the first quarter of 1997, subject to regulatory approval. It has already been approved by both companies' boards.
